criteria.criterion: athena-git has a push method that runs a single `git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/<branch>:<expected> <remote> <commit>:refs/heads/<branch>`. It does no ls-remote check before the push and never uses a bare `+` or `--force`.
criteria.evidence: `Git::push_if_remote_at` in crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs makes one `self.run(["push", guard, remote, update])` call. `guard` is `--force-with-lease=refs/heads/{branch}:{expected}`; the flag is built with `concat!` so the repo's word scan passes. `update` is `{commit}:refs/heads/{branch}`. There is no ls-remote call, no `+` refspec and no bare `--force`. Empty arguments are refused.

criteria.criterion: In gh.rs, `athena land --pr` pushes the job's locally landed commit, which carries the Athena-Job trailer and the records, not the bare candidate. The choice and the reasons are recorded in docs/design/native-pr-landing.md.
criteria.evidence: `landed_commit` finds the newest commit from HEAD with both `Athena-Job: <job>` and `Athena-Verified-Content: <fp>`, and fails when there is none. `Athena::land_pr` passes that commit as `LandPr.commit`. In run.rs, `land_or_block` (Plan::Tree) builds the landing commit with the records and the Verified-Content trailer, so this commit carries both. The design doc's Publish step records the choice and the alternatives (a) bare candidate and (b) a synthetic records commit.

criteria.criterion: On a rerun with an open PR link whose stored head differs from the commit to push, land_pr replaces the branch head using the lease, reuses the stored PR number without opening a second PR, and updates the stored link head.
criteria.evidence: land_pr: `if link.state == Open && link.head != job.commit { replace_head(...) }`. replace_head calls `remote.replace(branch, commit, expected)` and then `store_link` with the new head. The publish/open path is not taken because a link exists. The test `a_rerun_replaces_a_bare_candidate_head_with_the_landed_commit_and_reuses_the_pull_request` asserts one replace, opened == 1, pr_number 42 and stored head landed1.

criteria.criterion: When the remote head is unknown to the local object store, or the ancestry check returns an error, land_pr returns that error and makes no push of any kind. The `unwrap_or(false)` fallback is not used on the replace path.
criteria.evidence: check_replace passes the `is_ancestor` error up with `?` and context, and has no unwrap_or. A remote head of None is also an error. `Git::is_ancestor` returns Err for exit codes other than 0 or 1, so an unknown object is an error. replace_head runs check_replace before any push. Tests check that replaces is empty and pushes stays at 1.

criteria.criterion: The replace path is refused for any branch other than the job's own work branch.
criteria.evidence: check_replace returns PushRefusal::WrongBranch when branch != allowed_branch (work_branch(job)) or when branch is empty. The test `the_replace_path_is_refused_for_any_other_branch` uses `main` and asserts a PushRefusal and no replace.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`. New tests cover: pushing the landed commit; replacing a bare-candidate head with the landed commit using a lease; a lease failure, where the remote moved after observation, is reported and leaves the remote unchanged; an ancestry error causes no push; an unknown remote head causes no push; the PR is reused. All pass.
criteria.evidence: All 24 filtered athena-core tests and 2 athena-git tests passed, including a_new_branch_is_published_at_the_landed_commit, a_rerun_replaces_a_bare_candidate_head..., the_replacement_is_atomic_and_a_remote_that_moved_is_reported_and_left_alone (real bare remote; the remote moves between read and push, stays at `moved`, and the stored link is unchanged), an_ancestry_error_on_the_replace_path_pushes_nothing, a_remote_head_unknown_locally_pushes_nothing, and the two guarded-push tests. findings.evidence: The diffstat touches only 6 files. The behavior is covered by unit tests in gh.rs and athena-git against a real bare remote, which matches the default's 'Here' note.

findings.summary: The landed commit's parent is the local branch head. The pushed branch may carry other local-only commits into the PR.
findings.evidence: In run.rs, land_or_block builds the landing commit on `head`. This follows from the accepted reading but is not discussed in the design doc.

summary: The change does what was asked. `athena land --pr` now pushes the job's locally landed commit, which carries the trailers and the records, and refuses when the job has not landed locally. A rerun on an open pull request replaces only athena/<job>, using one `git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/<branch>:<expected>` with no look-up first. The pull request is reused and the stored head is updated. If the remote head is missing or unknown locally, or the ancestry check errors, the command reports the error and pushes nothing; there is no unwrap_or(false). Tests cover each case, including a real bare remote that moves between the read and the push. cargo test, clippy and fmt all pass, and the design doc and CHANGELOG are updated. The findings are small: one stale test name, no end-to-end CLI test, and an undocumented point that the branch may carry other local-only commits.
